To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the residual effects of crop residues on crop production and selected soil properties were prolonged and increased with increasing residue amounts.
the long-term (10-yr) residual effects of crop residues on grain production and selected soil properties are positive and proportional to the amount of residues previously returned.
the residual effects of crop residues on grain production are prolonged (10 yr), increase with increasing residue amount, and are not affected by time, tillage, N fertilization, or cover crop.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of crop residues on the soil environment, crop production and the environment.
the effects of crop residues on the environment.
developing management practices that improve soil properties and enhance crop production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the residual effect of crop residues is a function of the amount of residues returned to the soil, and is not a simple linear relationship.
the residual effects of crop residues are positive and long-term, and are enhanced by the amount of residue returned to the soil.
the residual effect of crop residue management on crop production is positive and that the effect is prolonged.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
crop residue management can have residual effects that are beneficial to subsequent crop production for a decade or more.
returning crop residue at a level that matches the amount produced by the previous year's crop is an effective management practice to improve soil and crop productivity.
the residual effects of returning crop residues at a 150% rate increased grain production and soil nutrient availability, but the residual effects of lower amounts were not as beneficial.
The main takeaway from our work is that
returning more crop residue than the previous year's crop can improve soil properties, which may benefit future crop production.
returning crop residues can enhance crop yields and soil quality for many years.
the amount of crop residues returned affects soil properties, which in turn, influence crop growth.
